backlogged.summary: In verify's finally block, the cleanup `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune` now throw HarnessError(git) when they time out. Such a throw can replace the original verify error or result. Consider catching cleanup timeouts, as the other cleanup errors are already ignored.

`lib/commands/approve.mjs` runs `git config user.email` through spawnSync with no time limit, so it uses neither budget.git_timeout_sec nor any other cap. It is not a verify, eval or run git call, so it is outside AC-1.

The F31 tests depend on wall-clock timing (sleep 5 with step_timeout_sec 3, a 15 s hang budget, a 3 s kill window). The first `harness verify` run of the full suite failed and was marked flaky. It passed 703/703 when run again, so the timing margins remain a load-sensitivity risk. Related to B177 and B185.
The Windows path is untested. Every fake-git test returns early when the platform is not POSIX, so tree-kill and git timeout behaviour on Windows have no coverage.

The verify.mjs base-worktree cleanup in `finally` (`worktree remove --force`, `worktree prune`) now throws gitTimeoutError when it times out, where before it returned a result. If the main body already threw (for example a `worktree add` timeout or a check error), a cleanup timeout replaces the original error, and `fs.rmSync` of baseDir is skipped when `remove` throws. The error code is still `git`, but the message can name the cleanup subcommand instead of the one that actually failed. Consider catching cleanup errors separately.

In runFeatures, gitOpts.timeoutSec is set only after validateUser. Any core git call made before that point uses the runner's default of 300 s, not the configured budget.git_timeout_sec, and an injected deps.git receives {timeoutSec: undefined}. Today this is harmless because no git call happens before config resolution, but the ordering invariant is implicit.

The full-suite verify command was reported flaky (exit 1 on one run). A local re-run of `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"` exited 0. Timing-dependent tests remain a source of flakes: the F31 AC-1 tests use 3 s and 5 s sleeps, and the F31 SC-1 tests use a 15 s hang budget with a 3 s liveness window.

Every POSIX-only F31 test (fake git shebang script) returns early on Windows, so on the Windows CI leg the process-tree kill for core git timeouts (SC-1) and the timeout message (AC-3) are not exercised end to end. Only killTree's taskkill path covers Windows.
